title: Computing on the extracted payload
statement: Let $M_g$ be a finite Turing machine that computes a total function $g$ on Boolean words within time bound $T_g$, and suppose $T_g$ is monotone. Then the buffered composition of the pair-component extractor and $M_g$ computes the function that sends each Boolean word $x$ to $g(b)$, where $b$ is the second component returned by the aligned pair parser on $x$, taken to be the empty word if parsing is undefined. On inputs of length $n$, this computation finishes within $6(n+1)+T_g(n)+1$ steps.
replaced:
Let a machine compute the total function $g$ within a monotone time bound
$T_g$. Then the buffered composition of the second-component pair extractor
with that machine computes, within $6(n+1) + T_g(n) + 1$ steps on inputs of
length $n$, the function sending $x$ to $g(b)$, where $b$ is the second
component of $x$ under the self-delimiting pair code (the empty word when $x$
is malformed).
